research_metadata.research_purpose: Technical deep dive to identify differentiation opportunities for SkillRunner

executive_summary.factory_positioning: Enterprise-focused AI coding agent platform ('agent-native software development') targeting organizations with 5,000+ engineers. Primary focus on collaborative-to-delegative workflow transition with strong emphasis on production incident response and backlog management.
executive_summary.key_finding: Factory.ai and SkillRunner serve fundamentally different use cases. Factory is an end-to-end development platform competing with Cursor/GitHub Copilot, while SkillRunner is a cost-optimization orchestration layer that could theoretically run ON TOP of Factory (using BYOK mode).
executive_summary.critical_insight: Factory has NO built-in cost tracking or optimization layer - they use abstracted 'Standard Tokens' with model multipliers. SkillRunner's per-phase, per-model cost tracking with actual vs premium comparison is a massive gap Factory cannot easily fill.
executive_summary.strategic_recommendation: Position SkillRunner as the 'FinOps layer for AI coding agents' - a tool that wraps Factory, Cursor, Copilot, etc. to add cost tracking, intelligent routing, and multi-provider orchestration.

final_recommendations.strategic_direction: Position SkillRunner as cost optimization infrastructure for AI development, NOT as a competitor to Factory
key_differentiators_to_emphasize: Per-phase cost tracking with actual vs hypothetical comparisons (Factory cannot offer this without business model change)
Automatic intelligent routing with quality-based fallback (Factory requires manual model selection)
Open source MIT license with full transparency (Factory is closed source SaaS)
Local-first architecture with zero external dependencies (Factory requires Factory Bridge and cloud)
FinOps integration with exportable cost reports (Factory abstracts costs away)
features_to_avoid: IDE integration (competes directly with Factory, Cursor, Copilot - crowded market)
Full development environment (out of scope, dilutes value proposition)
Organizational memory (complex, low ROI, Factory's strength)
Factory skill format compatibility (different purposes, adds complexity)

target_segments: Cost-conscious developers using expensive cloud models
FinOps teams needing AI spend visibility
Platform engineering teams building AI infrastructure
